h: The Two Tablets Embrace Every Soul in the Covenant

p: We have discussed (on the previous Shabbos)
it is already "let the year and its blessings begin."
"You are standing today, all of you," etc.
וְאִיתָא בַּתִּיקּוּנִים (הַקְדָּמָה דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל קָם סָבָא)
And it is stated in the Tikkunim (Introduction, the passage beginning "Kam Sava"):
'your little ones, your wives, and your convert
who is in the midst of your camp,
from your woodchopper to your water-drawer'
"and from them the Ten Commandments were given," etc.
And this is along the lines of what we said
(and it was explained for Chag HaShavuos)
מַה שֶּׁאָמַר (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רעג, א)
though the Tablets were not given on Shabbos;
the words of Torah were fixed in the heart,
along the lines of what is said (Mishlei 3:3):
"Write them on the tablet of your heart."
וְהוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשַׁת יִשָּׁקֵנִי)
And this is as it says (Shir HaShirim Rabbah, on "Let him kiss me," 1:2)
the learning of Torah was implanted in their hearts,
and with the utterance "You shall not have"
the evil inclination was uprooted from their hearts.
corresponds to "the heart of the wise man, at his right";
are the sum of the words of Torah;
and the mitzvah of honoring parents
"so that it may be good for you,"
and "good" is none other than Torah;
and this is the Oral Torah,
and the matter was granted him,
And "You shall not have" and "You shall not take"
also belong to the right Tablet,
"sits between the two openings of the heart";
for the evil inclination can entice
even the heart of the wise man at his right,
for at times it makes darkness into light
as we find with Menasheh and Yarovam,
and showed justifications for their error,
that it was service for the sake of Heaven.
And therefore Yarovam expounded a hundred and three facets,
וְנֶגֶד זֶה מִצְוַת לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ
and opposite this is the mitzvah "You shall not have."
the evil inclination shows another facet,
that by this one exalts the Name of Heaven,
while in truth it is "in vain"
וְכׇל זֶה נִכְתַּב עַל הַלּוּחַ הַיְמִינִי
And all this was written on the right Tablet,
which is to uproot the bad
and to bring in the words of Torah,
in the heart of the wise man at his right.
and your officers, every man of Yisrael";
הַיְינוּ שֶׁכּוּלָּם יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
that is, they all have a portion in the words of Torah,
"An inheritance of the congregation of Yaakov."
And on the second Tablet the prohibitions were written,
which is to empty out the bad
from the heart of the fool at his left,
and this corresponds to the Oral Torah,
and as written in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21):
"From the right was given the Written Torah,
and from the left was given the Oral Torah";
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב קסז, א)
and as written in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 167a):
"'Let there be light' — this is the right;
'and there was light' — this is the left."
And corresponding to this, "your little ones, your wives," etc.,
who are not people of Torah;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם הֵם שַׁיָּיכִים לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
nevertheless they too belong to the words of Torah,
וְאָמַר מֵחוֹטֵב עֵצֶיךָ עַד שׁוֹאֵב מֵימֶךָ
And it says, "from your woodchopper to your water-drawer,"
and does not mention servants in general,
for the intent that we said,
כְּמוֹ בְּעֶבֶד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
as with the servant of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
And that it mentions here specifically
הוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּהַפְטוֹרָה זוֹ
is along the lines of what is said in this haftarah:
אִם אֶתֵּן אֶת דְּגָנֵךְ עוֹד מַאֲכָל וְגוֹמֵר
"I will no longer give your grain as food," etc.
שֶׁכׇּל הַסְּעוּדָּה קְרוּיָה עַל שֵׁם לֶחֶם
for the whole meal is called by the name of bread;
and it alludes that they too
which is the aspect of bread,
as it says, "Come, eat of my bread,"
"and this is the bread of the Written Torah";
נֶגֶד וּשְׁתוּ בְּיַיִן מָסָכְתִּי (מִשְׁלֵי ט, ה)
correspond to "and drink of the wine I have mixed" (Mishlei 9:5),
וְהַתּוֹרָה נִמְשְׁלָה לְכׇל הַמַּשְׁקִים (תַּעֲנִית ז, א)
And the Torah is likened to all the beverages (Taanis 7a),
and goes to a low place;
"A sign of arrogance is poverty," etc.:
And this is why it says, "from your woodchopper," etc.:
the preparation of actual bread and water,
the bread leads to the Written Torah
and the water to the Oral Torah,
since they support the words of Torah,
נִכְלָל בָּהֶם גַּם כֵּן הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
the words of Torah are included in them as well.
for all agree that the Torah was given on Shabbos,
וְשַׁבָּת זְמַן הַשְׁפָּעַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
and Shabbos is the time of the bestowal of the Oral Torah,
as has been explained several times;
therefore this parshah is read on Shabbos.
